Set Residual Distribution Functions for Hawkes Model Specification

Source: R/hspec.R
set_residual.Rd

Attach residual density, distribution, quantile, and random-generation functions to an hspec object, with named parameter defaults for simulation and estimation.

Usage

set_residual(
  object,
  param,
  dresidual = NULL,
  presidual = NULL,
  qresidual = NULL,
  rresidual = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'hspec'
set_residual(
  object,
  param,
  dresidual = NULL,
  presidual = NULL,
  qresidual = NULL,
  rresidual = NULL
)

Arguments

object

An object of class hspec (Hawkes model specification)

param

A named numeric vector of residual-distribution parameters. Names match the declared formal arguments of the supplied distribution functions. For estimation, the values supply starting points rather than fixed constants.

dresidual

Density function of the residual distribution (optional)

presidual

Cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the residual distribution (optional)

qresidual

Quantile function of the residual distribution (optional)

rresidual

Random generation function of the residual distribution (optional)

...

Additional arguments for future extensions

Value

An updated hspec object with residual functions set

Details

The updated specification represents a model with the supplied residual distribution. Functions left NULL retain their existing slots. Supply consistent density and CDF functions for likelihood evaluation, a quantile function for residual inference, and a random generator for simulation.

The param argument in these functions defaults to the parameters provided during setup and is used for estimation. Only parameter names declared by each supplied distribution function are forwarded. Matching names across the wrapped functions share one estimated parameter. fitted_hspec() updates the residual generator when its named defaults match estimated coefficient names. Density wrappers accept log; CDF and quantile wrappers accept lower.tail and log.p. These options are forwarded when the supplied distribution supports them. User-defined distributions should provide log-density and upper-tail log-probability options to retain accuracy in extreme tails.

See also

logLik(), hfit(), fitted_hspec(), dtzexp()

Examples

# Create basic Hawkes specification
hspec_obj <- new("hspec",
                 mu = matrix(0.1, nrow = 1),
                 alpha = matrix(0.5, nrow = 1),
                 beta = matrix(1.0, nrow = 1))

# Set residual distribution parameters
params <- c(a = 0.5, ell = 1.0)

# Apply residual functions
hspec_obj <- set_residual(
  hspec_obj,
  param = params,
  dresidual = dtzexp,
  presidual = ptzexp,
  qresidual = qtzexp,
  rresidual = rtzexp
)

# Check resulting functions
hspec_obj@dresidual
#> function (x, param = c(a = 0.5, ell = 1), log = FALSE) 
#> {
#>     residual_density(dresidual, x, log = log, params = distribution_parameters(dresidual, 
#>         param))
#> }
#> <environment: 0x55dbe134fc98>
hspec_obj@rresidual
#> function (size, param = c(a = 0.5, ell = 1)) 
#> {
#>     do.call(rresidual, c(list(size), distribution_parameters(rresidual, 
#>         param)))
#> }
#> <environment: 0x55dbe134fc98>
hspec_obj@dresidual(c(0.2, 1), log = TRUE)
#> [1] -0.1932906 -1.0007753
hspec_obj@presidual(c(0.2, 1), lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
#> [1] -0.1977121 -1.0007753
